title: Burlingame
name: Burlingame
metaTitle: 1031 Exchange Burlingame CA | 1031 Exchange San Francisco
metaDescription: Burlingame 1031 exchange coordination for airport-corridor hotel, auto row, and retail owners along the Bayshore Highway and El Camino Real.

sections.html: Burlingame's investment map is basically drawn by SFO's flight paths on one side and Burlingame Avenue's shopping district on the other, and the two barely overlap. I have sat in enough hotel engineering offices along Bayshore Highway to know that a change of ownership here means something very different depending on which side of that map the property sits on. A retail buyer on Burlingame Avenue is thinking about foot traffic and lease term; a hotel buyer three blocks away is thinking about brand standards and flight schedules, and neither one benefits from the other's advisor team.

sections.heading: The Airport Sets the Terms of This Corridor
sections.html:
Burlingame's commercial stock is unusually specialized for a city its size, and each type carries its own operating rhythm:

  • Branded hotels along Bayshore Highway serving SFO travelers
  • Auto dealership and service properties along El Camino Real and California Drive
  • Upscale retail along Burlingame Avenue and Broadway
  • Caltrain-adjacent office space near the downtown core
  • Light-industrial and service-commercial parcels closer to the freeway

Flight volume out of SFO has a direct pull on hotel occupancy here, and a facilities team running one of these properties feels that pull in staffing and maintenance scheduling long before it shows up in a quarterly revenue report.

sections.heading: Identifying Across a Specialized Market
sections.html: Because hotel product and auto dealership real estate don't compare cleanly to retail or office, a seller exiting one of those specialized assets often needs the 200% rule to name candidates across categories. A seller trading Burlingame Avenue retail for another retail asset nearby can usually keep it simple with the three-property rule. I still ask every seller to write the identification list with the qualified intermediary rather than a broker, since the legal description on a hotel or dealership parcel is often more complicated than a standard retail lot.

sections.heading: The Downtime a Brand Flag Actually Requires
sections.html: A branded hotel doesn't change hands without a property improvement plan from the franchisor, and that PIP almost always means guest room and common-area downtime that a buyer's operations team needs scheduled before closing, not discovered after. On the auto row side, a dealership's service bay closures for equipment upgrades or a franchise-required remodel carry the same logic: get the contractor's real timeline before you assume the property cash-flows on day one under new ownership. A PIP scope that looks like a modest line item in a broker's summary can turn into a floor-by-floor renovation once the franchisor's inspector actually walks the property.

sections.heading: Coordinating a Franchise Transfer With the Exchange Clock
sections.html: Hotel franchise transfers and dealership franchise agreements both run on their own approval timelines, and those timelines don't care about the 45-day identification window or the 180-day exchange period. I keep the qualified intermediary, lender, and franchisor approval process moving in parallel rather than in sequence, because waiting for one to finish before starting the next is how Burlingame closings slip past their deadline. Franchisor paperwork almost always takes longer than either party expects, so I push buyers to submit that application the same week they sign the purchase agreement rather than waiting for financing to firm up first.

sections.heading: What Works in This Corridor
sections.html: The investors who do well here go in knowing exactly which specialized asset class they're buying, hotel, auto, retail, or office, and line up the right operator and lender conversations for that category early rather than treating a Burlingame purchase like a generic commercial deal. A generic diligence checklist borrowed from a standard retail purchase will miss almost everything that actually matters on a hotel or dealership closing here.

faqs.q: Does a hotel PIP requirement affect the 1031 exchange timeline?
faqs.a: It can, since franchisor approval and improvement scope need to be understood before closing, and the required work often means real downtime for guest rooms or common areas. Getting that scope in writing early keeps the 180-day exchange period from becoming a scramble.

faqs.q: Is auto dealership real estate a good 1031 replacement for a Burlingame retail seller?
faqs.a: It can diversify a portfolio well, but the franchise agreement, service bay layout, and environmental considerations around fuel and fluid storage all need separate diligence from a standard retail purchase. That's worth raising with the investor's advisor team before it goes on an identification list.

faqs.q: How many replacement properties should I identify if I'm exiting a hotel here?
faqs.a: More than three is typical, since comparable hotel product is limited and an investor often wants to name retail or office alternatives alongside other hotel candidates. The 200% rule accommodates that mixed list better than the three-property rule.

faqs.q: What should a buyer check before closing on Burlingame Avenue retail?
faqs.a: Lease term and tenant sales performance matter most on this stretch, since foot traffic depends heavily on the retail mix staying strong block to block. A walkthrough of the storefront's condition alongside the lease file is worth doing before the identification deadline, not after. Parking availability nearby also deserves a look, since it affects how much of that foot traffic converts into repeat customers for the tenant.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange San Francisco confirm a hotel or dealership purchase qualifies for exchange?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates identification, scheduling, and communication among the investor's advisors. Whether a specific property and transaction qualify is a determination made by the investor's CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary, particularly where a franchise agreement or improvement plan changes the underlying real property analysis.
